title: Grateful Dead Live at Vanderbilt University on 1972-10-21
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC -> Remastering -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard capture of a thrilling first‑show performance, highlighted by an exceptional, jam‑filled “He's Gone.”
ai_review.review: The recording offers a clear enough soundboard mix that lets Phil’s bass shine—far better than many ’66 tapes—while the show itself is remembered as a magical first Dead concert. Reviewers rave about the sweet Jerry solo on “He’s Gone,” even quoting “First There Is a Mountain,” and overall describe the night as an unforgettable, high‑energy experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently positive comments about both the musical performance (standout Jerry solo, memorable first show) and the recording quality (clearer than typical ’66 tapes), yielding a high weighted average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audio is described as fine and clearer than most 1966 recordings; Phil’s bass is audible throughout, indicating a solid soundboard mix with no major issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fans recall the concert as a memorable inaugural show with strong energy and smooth transitions throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Obscenely sweet jamming on “He’s Gone,” including a ‘First There Is a Mountain’ quotation around the twelve‑minute mark.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is clear and prominent, praised for being audible where it often isn’t in other recordings from this era.
